terms.definition: A coherent system part whose goal and interface form a reusable public Sigil contract.
A declaration that contributes operational detail to a matching component without overriding its public contract or other expands.
The goal, interface, and public concept identities that a component exposes to dependents.
A reusable identity grouping collective semantic-line occurrences across a component and its matching expands; it is public when it occurs in interface.
A non-empty line of Sigil prose expressing one distinct semantic idea.
The aggregate of separately sourced operational contributions from every expand matching a component.
The strict .sigil/config.json file that declares a workspace's language version, boundary, source selection, and tool configuration.
The configured Sigil workspace selected and governed by its eligible ConfigFile.
The workspace root or a declared workspace member that requires an ordinary Brownfield summary component.
An included #module.sigil file that defines intentional directory-import shorthand without controlling workspace membership or component visibility.
The local components and successfully resolved directly imported names exposed by a ModuleIndexFile.
The optional strict .sigil/glossary.json file containing reviewed workspace and bounded-context terminology.
A path-scoped glossary domain whose terms may replace workspace spellings for sources matched by that context alone.
An approved Sigil semantic contract whose wording governs when it conflicts with glossary prose or implementation evidence.
A design workflow used when no existing implementation constrains the selected behavior or component.
An adoption workflow used when relevant implementation exists but Sigil coverage is absent, incomplete, ambiguous, or potentially drifted.
The reusable workflow that determines whether a repository mutation is blocked, requires review, or is ready from the exact action, scope, change set, applicable evidence, and explicit user approval.
The version literal governing interpretation of Sigil source and workspace configuration.
The version of a distributable CLI, core, LSP, skill, or editor artifact, owned by that artifact's manifest independently from LanguageVersion.
The directory containing the eligible ConfigFile that defines a Sigil workspace.
A non-root project boundary explicitly declared by workspace.members within the same configured Sigil workspace.
An import whose path selects a directory and resolves named components through that directory's ModuleIndexFile.
The source spelling used to denote a Sigil concept identity.
The flat set of local and accessible concept identities resolved for a component and all of its matching expands.
A consumer-local occurrence of a concept that preserves the concept's originating identity while recording its use in the current component context.
Structural, configuration, workspace, resolution, graph, projection, and diagnostic facts reproducibly computed by compatible Sigil tools without model-assisted judgment.
Host-assisted interpretation of intent, rationale, readiness, conflicts, or design quality that remains subject to explicit human review.
An exact start-to-end location interval within a Sigil or configuration source.
A source-faithful recovered Sigil document that retains usable declarations and semantic content despite structural diagnostics.

A filesystem or runtime failure from the host environment; a required-operation host failure propagates to the caller, while a failure during optional enrichment may become a diagnostic when a meaningful primary result remains available.
Host-side work that augments an already meaningful primary result and may be omitted with a structured diagnostic when it fails.
A recognized canonical term or alias in free-form Sigil prose, linked to its effective glossary entry and exact source range.
The deterministic workspace-wide view of resolved glossary contexts, entries, source occurrences, and diagnostics.
The scoped subset of a glossary projection relevant to selected Sigil sources and their related expansion sources.
A glossary entry applicable to a particular Sigil source after workspace and bounded-context resolution.

A deterministic projection for a selected component that includes its complete Sigil description together with each direct dependency's public contract and durable decision rationale, while excluding transitive and other private dependency content by default.
Required by the decision record convention; states the selected course or outcome whose rationale is being recorded.
Required by the decision record convention; states the governed boundary and important exclusions.
States materially applicable conditions treated as true when making the decision.
States materially applicable benefits, costs, and tensions accepted by the decision.
States materially applicable problems or pressures the decision resolves.
States materially relevant options not selected and why they were rejected.
States materially applicable effects and obligations created by the decision.
States conditions that should trigger reconsideration of the decision.
Source code, configuration, migrations, scripts, workflow instructions, tests, fixtures, metadata, validators, generated assets, or documentation governed as part of implementation.
A creation, modification, move, or deletion of an implementation artifact; excludes read-only inspection and exact user-requested rollback of the current agent's unapproved changes.
A process-local, workspace-root-scoped collection of supported implementation-source contents reused for ownership queries until a supported source or the workspace root changes.
A section name in an implementation ownership annotation that identifies an implementation-related section occurrence on the targeted component or concept.
ConfigFile include and exclude rules applied to determine which Sigil source documents belong to a loaded workspace.
Selection of the installation-relative skill assets owned by the Sigil executable or source module chosen for installation.
A provisional skill-assessed state indicating that no unresolved material semantic, architectural, or design problem remains within the reviewed Sigil scope.
A dedicated same-chat workflow state that pauses ordinary Sigil design or review while a material semantic, architectural, or design problem is explained and resolved with the user.
The reviewed authoring activity that groups coherent interface semantic lines under new or reusable concept identifiers.
Model-assisted inspection of semantically ready Sigil prose for material project vocabulary, ambiguity, and conflicting usage without granting glossary authority.
A new or changed binding choice whose rationale or excluded alternatives cannot be safely reconstructed during future review, maintenance, or implementation.

The reviewed mapping of each material selected choice to a decisions occurrence preserving durable rationale, or to a justified omission for a trivial, mechanically derived, or safely reconstructable choice.
Concise project reasoning needed for future review, maintenance, or implementation and preserved in Sigil decisions rather than session transcripts.

A conversation-scoped, nonbinding record of an external-guidance investigation containing its question, source authority and identity, applicability, environment match, findings, limitations, conflicts, and freshness conditions.
